title: Scheduler integration: consume KV cache eviction/pressure signals (no starvation) + document contract
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Goal
Integrate the new KV cache allocator/eviction system with the runtime scheduler so that:
- Scheduler can react to memory pressure (fragmentation/allocation failures/eviction requests) without causing starvation or pathological oscillation.
- Overload behavior is explicit and predictable across tenant tiers/SLA classes.
- Contract between scheduler <-> KV cache is documented (signals, required invariants, concurrency assumptions).

Context
Under bursty traffic and mixed seq lengths, KV cache fragmentation increases allocation churn and tail latency. Compaction/eviction introduces new failure modes if scheduler keeps admitting work when allocator is already in a degraded state, or if eviction selection interacts poorly with fairness (e.g., evicting the same tenant repeatedly).

Scope
1) Signals + plumbing
- Add a scheduler-visible "cache pressure" signal emitted by KV cache / allocator.
- Add an explicit callback/hook for allocator to request eviction/backpressure when allocation would fail or fragmentation ratio crosses trigger threshold.
- Propagate request metadata needed for fair victim selection (tenant, tier, route/model family, request age).

2) Scheduler policy changes (no starvation)
- Update admission control and batch formation logic to incorporate cache pressure.
- Implement guardrails so lower-tier traffic is slowed under pressure, but not indefinitely starved when system recovers.
- Ensure dedicated pools with strict SLA classes maintain guarantees: allow preemption/backpressure of lower-priority queues before evicting higher-tier active sequences.

3) Contract + invariants doc (in ticket + Confluence link)
- Define what each component may assume:
  - Scheduler must not hold allocator locks while awaiting GPU sync.
  - Allocator must provide monotonic-ish pressure signal with hysteresis to avoid thrash.
  - Eviction requests must be idempotent and safe under concurrent decode/prefill.
  - "No starvation" definition and the specific implementation (see acceptance criteria).

Out of scope
- Changing eviction policy itself (ENG-2845) beyond any required metadata wiring.
- Changing compaction trigger thresholds/budgets (ENG-2847), except to read the resulting pressure state.

Implementation sketch
- Add CachePressureState { level: OK|WARM|HOT|CRITICAL, frag_ratio, alloc_fail_rate, last_transition_ts } exposed via a lock-free snapshot.
- Scheduler loop consumes snapshot once per scheduling tick and adjusts:
  - Admission tokens / max inflight sequences
  - Decode batch target size
  - Prefill concurrency (more aggressive reduction vs decode under pressure)
- Add hysteresis:
  - HOT -> WARM requires sustained recovery window (e.g., 30s) to prevent oscillation.
- Starvation protection:
  - When in WARM/HOT, apply weighted backoff by tier rather than a hard block.
  - Maintain per-tenant minimum service rate (configurable floor) unless in CRITICAL.
  - In CRITICAL: allow hard shed for lowest tier, but require "recovery probe" scheduling (periodic small admits) once allocator returns to HOT/WARM.

Artifacts
- Primary design: Confluence draft in "kv-cache-compaction-improvements-design-v1" (section: Scheduler integration + contract)
- ADR reference: ADR-0129 (eviction policy + scheduler contract)
- Expected PR: redwood/pr-18463 (scheduler integration + cache pressure signal)
acceptance_criteria: A scheduler-visible cache pressure signal is available (exported snapshot) and is consumed on each scheduling tick without adding >1% overhead to scheduling hot path (bench + flamegraph evidence).

Under synthetic pressure scenarios (forced allocation failures / high fragmentation), scheduler reduces admission/prefill concurrency and avoids allocator thrash (no repeated alloc-fail loop > N occurrences/minute; N agreed with SRE).

No starvation: in WARM/HOT states, lower-tier traffic continues to make progress (measurable: each active tenant queue receives service within a bounded window when there is available capacity; document the bound and how measured).
In CRITICAL state, policy is explicit and deterministic: lowest tier may be shed/throttled first; higher tiers preserved as long as feasible; behavior documented and gated behind runtime flag config.
Scheduler/allocator contract is documented (signals, invariants, failure modes) and linked in this ticket; reviewed by Runtime Architect (Noah Patel) and SRE rollout owner (Sean Gallagher).

Integration tests added/updated: multi-tenant burst mix with varying context lengths shows reduced p99 spikes vs baseline when compaction is enabled, with no regression in fairness metrics (tenant starvation checks).

Metrics emitted with correct labels (region, pool, model_family, tenant_tier): cache_pressure_level, scheduler_admission_throttle_ratio, eviction_requests_total, alloc_failures_total; dashboards can be built off these.
Feature-flag behavior: with compaction disabled, cache pressure defaults to OK and scheduler behavior is unchanged (verified via A/B test in perf suite).
comments: 2025-02-18 (Talia Benson): Marking P0 given customer escalations tied to tail latency + allocator churn. Please keep SRE (Sean/Rafael) in the loop on overload behavior; we need clear rollback levers.

2025-02-20 (Sofia Ivanova): Started wiring a lightweight CachePressureState snapshot from allocator -> scheduler. Plan is to avoid locks: allocator writes to an atomic struct once per interval; scheduler reads each tick. Need to align on label set with Logan (telemetry).

2025-02-22 (Julian Moore): Looked at existing admission control. We currently gate mostly on GPU util + inflight seq count; adding a third "memory pressure" axis will require retuning prefill concurrency specifically (prefill allocates KV quickly). I’ll add a local sim for oscillation tests.

2025-02-25 (Sean Gallagher): For canary, please define hard rollback triggers (alloc_failures_total > baseline + X%, p99 decode > Y ms sustained 15m). Also want a "pressure stuck HOT" alert (time in HOT > 30m).

2025-02-27 (Noah Patel): Contract needs to be very explicit about what scheduler can do when allocator says CRITICAL. Suggest: scheduler must stop admitting new prefills immediately, allow in-flight decodes to drain if possible, and only shed lowest tier if alloc failures persist. Also document concurrency: eviction/compaction may run on a separate stream; scheduler must not assume immediate recovery after a state transition.

2025-03-02 (Sofia Ivanova): Implemented hysteresis transitions locally (HOT->WARM requires 30s stable; WARM->OK requires 60s). Added per-tier throttling multipliers (hosted free > pro > enterprise > dedicated). Still need to prove non-starvation under prolonged HOT (sim + integration test).

2025-03-05 (Sofia Ivanova): PR draft up with cache pressure signal + scheduler hook (will become pr-18463). Remaining: fairness floor (min service rate) implementation + doc pass in Confluence + review from SRE.
